title: Independent adult front-leg femur–tibia validation evidence
scope: Compact factual observations and protocols required to evaluate the existing browser-local muscle, joint and FeCO model. This is not a redistribution of raw recordings.

preparation.extrapolation: No record in this artifact validates middle or hind legs.

roleDefinitions.fit: Known constraint that informed version 3.5 or may be used for parameter fitting.
roleDefinitions.held-out: Not used by the 3.5 constraint validator or frozen constants; evaluated before any 3.6 tuning.
roleDefinitions.audit-only: A factual boundary or qualitative observation that must be reported but is not a scalar fit target.
roleDefinitions.context: Protocol or interpretation needed to avoid a category or unit error.

evidenceClassDefinitions.reported-scalar: A number stated in article text, caption or methods.
evidenceClassDefinitions.publisher-figure-digitized: Coordinates extracted from a publisher-rendered figure with declared calibration uncertainty; never raw data.
evidenceClassDefinitions.raw-derived: A value recomputed from a source raw-data product with a recorded method and hash.
evidenceClassDefinitions.engineering: A preregistered model-evaluation rule, not a biological measurement.

protocols.reference: Methods: Moving the tibia/pin using a magnetic control system; Figures 2 and 4
protocols.notes: The article reports no acceleration for the swing command. The generator therefore uses constant-speed ramps and does not invent one.

protocols.reference: Methods: Moving the tibia/pin using a magnetic control system; Figures 5 and 7
protocols.notes: The paper reports small deviations between commanded and actual tibia motion. The browser generator represents the command and labels it as such.

protocols.reference: Results: position and velocity tuning; Methods: swing motion trials; Figure S5
protocols.notes: The methods list commanded speeds; the results describe the approximate measured speed range. They are retained separately.
The current 100 Hz body loop can carry only an envelope and cannot represent this carrier.

protocols.reference: Results: A gradient of force per spike; Figure 4
protocols.fastIntermediateStimulation: 10–20 ms optogenetic flashes of increasing intensity
protocols.slowStimulation: 500 ms somatic current steps; additional spikes above resting firing
protocols.notes: Absolute-force comparison requires a spike/activity bridge and the probe observation model.

observations.reference: Results paragraph P22; Figure 4B; Methods direction selectivity
observations.measurement: GCaMP6f delta-F/F from R64C04-Gal4 club axon regions
observations.observationModel: Compare direction ratio first on FeCO drive. This is a representation-level proxy, not a claim that drive equals fluorescence.
observations.metric: (maximum flexion response - maximum extension response) / their sum; maxima during six 8.01 Hz imaging frames after movement onset
observations.uncertainty: Reported mean±SEM; movement-to-imaging frame alignment is unavailable in the compact artifact.
observations.extraction: Direct article-text transcription; no plot digitization.

observations.measurement: Steady-state claw GCaMP6f near 90 degrees
observations.observationModel: Normalize modeled end-of-hold claw channels to their own protocol maxima.

value.description: Neither flexion nor extension population is active close to 90 degrees.

observations.metric: maximum normalized claw response at 90±9 degrees
observations.uncertainty: Article reports the property qualitatively; the numerical gate is engineering and deliberately loose.
observations.extraction: Direct article-text transcription; no curve coordinates used.

observations.measurement: End-of-hold normalized claw GCaMP6f versus joint angle
observations.observationModel: Separate regression of activating-direction flexion and extension branches away from the midpoint.

value.description: Population activity increases as a relatively linear function away from approximately 90 degrees.

observations.metric: minimum R-squared of the two branch regressions
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative source statement; the numerical gate is engineering.
observations.extraction: Direct article-text transcription; no curve coordinates used.

observations.measurement: Difference in normalized end-of-hold claw response at the same angle after opposite movement histories
observations.observationModel: Mean signed difference over 18–72 degrees for flexion claw and 108–162 degrees for extension claw.

value.description: Clear directional hysteresis remains in steady-state responses measured at the end of the hold.

observations.metric: mean activating-history minus opposite-history response, averaged across both claw branches
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative source statement; the positive numerical gate is engineering and does not fit the plot magnitude.
observations.extraction: Direct article-text transcription; no curve coordinates used.

observations.measurement: Club movement response across the joint range
observations.observationModel: Compare modeled peak club drive for equal-speed steps near 90 degrees and near full extension.

value.description: Responses occur throughout the range, are slightly larger around 90 degrees and smaller at 180 degrees.

observations.metric: mean central-step peak divided by full-extension-adjacent step peak
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative source statement; the numerical gate tests presence, not published magnitude.

observations.measurement: Maximum slope of hook GCaMP6f signal over the measured velocity series
observations.observationModel: Use normalized modeled hook peak as a transducer-level proxy; report the calcium representation mismatch.

value.description: Hook response slope is similar across the measured speed range.

observations.metric: maximum nonzero hook response divided by minimum across commanded speeds
observations.uncertainty: Source is qualitative and commanded speed differs from actual movement; numerical gate is engineering.

observations.measurement: Speed at maximum slope of club GCaMP6f signal
observations.observationModel: Modeled club movement-envelope peak speed.
observations.metric: commanded speed with maximum modeled club response
observations.uncertainty: Reported as approximately 400 degrees/s; no SEM supplied.

observations.measurement: Club GCaMP6f response to piezo-driven tibia vibration
observations.observationModel: No valid carrier-level observation model exists in the 100 Hz body loop.
observations.metric: must report not-evaluable until a high-rate vibration carrier and frequency-resolved club populations exist
observations.uncertainty: Population peaks are article statements; individual cells are diversely frequency tuned.

observations.observationModel: Modeled activation half-rise time; probe mechanics remain a systematic difference.

observations.observationModel: Modeled slow activation under sustained command.
observations.metric: rise remains incomplete at 500 ms and release effect has approximately 100 ms scale
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative/approximate article statements.

splitPolicy.notes: Audit-only and context records are not score targets. These roles describe version 3.6 fitting eligibility and may not be reassigned after baseline generation.

knownRepresentationLimits: FeCO output channels are normalized transducer drives, whereas the reported Mamiya measurements are GCaMP6f fluorescence at 8.01 Hz.
BANC generic claw/hook roots are not identical to the genetic-driver regions measured by Mamiya et al.
The 100 Hz body loop cannot reproduce 100–2000 Hz vibration carriers or tonotopic club responses.
Motor-unit inputs are normalized population activity rather than identified spike trains, and active force is relative rather than micronewtons.
The current joint lacks measured moment arms, tendon geometry, inertia and the Azevedo force-probe observation model.
